header.title: SpaceX O-RAN shift to Qualcomm chipsets benefits Qualcomm and base-station component suppliers

s01_bottom_line.text: SpaceX signed a multi-year agreement to adopt Qualcomm's Dragonwing 5G O-RAN base station chipsets for a US mobile network, moving away from Ericsson and Nokia; TrendForce names Amphenol, Qorvo, American Tower and Crown Castle as potential ecosystem beneficiaries.
TrendForce frames Qualcomm and its ecosystem partners (Amphenol, Qorvo, American Tower, Crown Castle) as primary beneficiaries and Ericsson/Nokia as displaced.

If the rollout across ~80,000 sites proceeds, Qualcomm captures chipset share from incumbent RAN vendors and named antenna, power-amplifier and tower suppliers gain new volume, though the article quantifies no revenue impact for any listed name.

items.text: SpaceX and Qualcomm announced a multi-year supply agreement for SpaceX to adopt Qualcomm's Dragonwing 5G base station chipset solutions.
SpaceX secured access to approximately 80,000 base station sites via leasing arrangements with independent tower operators. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
TrendForce projects the global 5G infrastructure market value will reach US$55 billion in 2027. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
SpaceX is expanding into the US mobile communications market, moving away from proprietary RAN architectures dominated by Ericsson and Nokia.
Qualcomm's O-RAN chipset approach could substantially reduce the cost of deploying tens of thousands of 5G base stations across the US.
Suppliers of 5G base station components are positioned to gain new business opportunities from the SpaceX-Qualcomm rollout.

s04_key_evidence.label: O-RAN operators have faced interoperability challenges when sourcing DUs, RUs and CUs from different vendors due to signal compatibility issues.
